headline: High-risk data and capability mismatch: Haystack’s broad egress/MCP can create leakage and cascading-action paths, while godot_rl_agents lacks shared surfaces so injection/conflict are limited.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared communication channel is documented between godot_rl_agents and Haystack. A has no io_surfaces and no network egress; B can call MCP servers, but without a shared bridge or file channel the pairwise injection pathway is not evidenced. Uncertainty does not justify inventing a bridge.
conditions: IF a shared filesystem, clipboard, or MCP bridge is added between the two agents, prompt-injection risk becomes plausible.
IF either agent begins parsing the other’s raw text as instructions, reassess upward.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Do not connect them through a shared clipboard or message queue.
Require explicit provenance tags on any exchanged text.
Review any MCP server allowlist before enabling it.

B_data_leakage.rationale: godot_rl_agents touches no data classes and has no network egress, while Haystack has broad egress and touches anonymous usage statistics. The pair does not show a shared workspace or sensitive data class, so leakage is limited; however, Haystack’s outbound connectivity makes accidental context export possible if shared inputs are introduced.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same workspace containing sensitive files, leakage risk increases.
IF Haystack is configured to ingest local file contents or prompts containing secrets, outbound exposure becomes plausible.
mitigations: Keep sensitive files out of Haystack inputs.
Use separate directories for each agent.
Disable or restrict outbound connectors in Haystack.
Redact secrets before passing text between agents.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: godot_rl_agents shows no write or network surfaces, while Haystack exposes REST APIs and MCP servers with broad egress. There is no documented overlapping write target or shared mutable resource, so direct capability conflict is not evidenced. The main risk is only if an orchestrator later maps both onto the same mutable backend.
conditions: IF both agents are granted write access to the same filesystem, database, or git repo, conflict risk rises.
IF an orchestrator adds locking-free shared state, reassess upward.
mitigations: Avoid giving both agents the same API credentials.
Add locking around any shared mutable resource.
Keep Haystack read-only unless writes are required.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Haystack can consume external inputs via REST/MCP and may act on them, while godot_rl_agents is a game-playing system that can generate outputs later fed into Haystack. If Haystack treats those outputs as authoritative, errors can cascade into downstream retrieval or actions. The interaction is inferred from documented surfaces, so uncertainty pushes this to medium.
conditions: IF Haystack uses godot_rl_agents output as a source document or tool result without verification, cascading error is active.
IF Haystack is connected to downstream actions such as ticketing, email, or database writes, impact increases.
mitigations: Insert a verification step before Haystack consumes A’s output.
Label A’s output as untrusted provenance.
Require human review for any downstream action.

E_compliance.rationale: No regulated data class is documented for godot_rl_agents, and Haystack only lists anonymous usage statistics. There is no evidence of residency, certification, or retention mismatch in this pair, so compliance risk is limited to generic policy drift rather than a concrete violation. The other agent is not cited because no regulated flow is shown.
conditions: IF regulated data such as PHI or EU PII is routed through Haystack, compliance review is required.
IF retention or residency settings differ between deployments, reassess upward.
mitigations: Confirm the data class before routing it.
Keep regulated data out of this pair unless controls are added.
